entry.content: ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) remove their private .filelock-* link directories with shutil.rmtree (a recursive delete) on a remembered path. entry.content: On Windows, ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) connect SQLite to the lock database by its path, in every directory. SQLite derives three side files from that path: <database>-journal, the rollback journal (pages saved to undo an interrupted write); <database>-wal, the write-ahead log (changes kept outside the main file); and <database>-shm, the shared-memory index of the WAL. entry.content: Impactserialize-javascript escapes its output so it is safe to embed inside a<script> element. entry.content: ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) hand SQLite a name they do not control. entry.content: Vulnerability summaryaddressparser ends an RFC 5322 group at the first ;, including one inside a quoted display name or a comment. The text after it is parsed again as top level recipients with the quoting flipped, so text that every conformant parser reads as a display name or comment becomes a live address. G: (a; <evil@evil.com>) <v@victim.com>; names only v@victim.com, and Nodemailer read it as the single recipient evil@evil.com. Affected: 3.0.0 through 10.1.3.Attacker capabilitiesThe attack

entry.content: Vulnerability summaryaddressparser ends an angle-addr at the first > it sees, including one inside a quoted local part, a comment or a domain literal. The domain is then read off the text in front of that >. <"a@evil.com>"@good.com> is the mailbox "a@evil.com>"@good.com under RFC 5322, and Nodemailer read it as an address at evil.com.
